source.name: Forex Factory
source.headline: Treasury Department to buy back $6 billion in longer-term debt, triple the normal level

learning_v2.note: No context-specific ACTIONABLE segment was used to override current macro facts; generic directional 5-6 confidence segments are KEEP_NEUTRAL.

predictions.mechanism: The $6B buyback was below some higher market expectations and the 10Y yield rose to about 4.83%, pressuring duration-sensitive technology valuations despite the liquidity-support intent.
predictions.invalidation: A sustained drop in US10Y/US2Y yields following the operation or a materially larger follow-up buyback would weaken the bearish signal.

predictions.mechanism: Higher long yields after the announcement offset the supportive liquidity signal, while oil above $100 keeps inflation risk elevated.
predictions.invalidation: A clear reversal lower in Treasury yields together with stable risk sentiment would invalidate the downside bias.

predictions.mechanism: The Dow is less duration-sensitive than NDX, leaving the buyback's liquidity support and higher-yield headwind more balanced.
predictions.invalidation: A sharp yield breakout higher would shift the balance toward DOWN; a sustained yield decline would shift it toward UP.

predictions.mechanism: Higher Treasury yields are a gold headwind, but dollar softness and elevated geopolitical/oil risk support safe-haven demand.
predictions.invalidation: A simultaneous sharp rise in DXY and real/nominal yields would turn the balance bearish for gold.
